newsitem.title: USA: Crop Growers says former executives to sell shares.
newsitem.headline: Crop Growers says former executives to sell shares.

text.p: Crop Growers Corp said former chief executive John Hemmingson has agreed to sell his 1.14 million common shares in the company to Great American Insurance Co of Cincinnati for $10 per share.
Notice of the sale was given under terms of an agreement between Hemmingson and Fireman's Fund Insurance Co under which Fireman's Fund has a right of first refusal on the sale of Hemmingson's shares.
Great American has also agreed to buy the 681,744 shares of Crop Growers' stock held by former chief financial officer Gary Black for $10 per share, the company said.
On a combined basis, Hemmingson and Black own 22.9 percent of Crop Growers' outstanding common shares.
Fireman's Fund has until March 6 to determine whether to exercise its right of first refusal, Crop Growers said.
State insurance regulatory approval is required to acquire over 10 percent of the company's stock.
Crop Growers markets and services federal multi-peril crop insurance and crop hail insurance for third party insurance companies and its own insurance company subsidiaries.
At December 31, the company had 7.97 million shares outstanding.
